source_caption:
The hilariously infuriating airplane sequence that kicks off the entire movie features a brilliant, hidden piece of personal casting. The fiercely passive-aggressive flight attendant who repeatedly ignores Dave’s polite requests for a headset, ultimately triggering the bizarre misunderstanding that gets him tased, is played by actress Jackie Titone. Behind the scenes, she wasn’t just a random comedic foil—she was Adam Sandler’s real-life fiancée. The two had been dating for years and actually got married exactly two months after the film’s theatrical release. By weaponizing their genuine, real-life connection to create an excruciatingly frustrating, perfectly executed comedic escalation, Sandler masterfully proves that sometimes the absolute best scene partners are the ones you trust enough to drive you completely insane.
⠀
Anger Management (2003), directed by Peter Segal, starring Adam Sandler, Jack Nicholson, Marisa Tomei. After a massively blown-out-of-proportion misunderstanding on a commercial flight, a mild-mannered businessman is unjustly sentenced to an intensive anger management program run by a highly unorthodox, deeply unhinged therapist who aggressively upends his entire life.

source_details.title: Anger Management
source_details.synopsis: Anger Management is a 2003 American comedy film directed by Peter Segal and written by David S. Dorfman. Starring Adam Sandler and Jack Nicholson with Marisa Tomei, Luis Guzmán, Woody Harrelson and John Turturro in supporting roles, the film tells the story of a businessman who is sentenced to an anger management program under a renowned therapist with unconventional methods. This was the final film role for Lynne Thigpen, who died weeks before its release and is dedicated in her memory. Released in theaters in the United States on April 11, 2003, by Sony Pictures Releasing, the film received mixed reviews from critics and grossed $195.7 million against a $75 million budget.
